Definition: from G202; an audience-room:--place of hearing.
BiblicalUsage: Once, when Festus brings Paul before Agrippa: on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city. The word is the audience room — the hall where the hearing happens.
TheologicalSignificance: A room name carries no teaching, and the word itself has none; its weight is the scene it frames, earthly pomp on one side and a chained apostle speaking the Word on the other.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
